meta.generatedBy: website-builder crawl, then hand-reconciled by parsing each route's real HTML snapshot: <main>'s direct children, with every top-level <section> collected and shared blocks confirmed by normalized-hash across all 21 routes.

categories.SHELL: Site chrome carried across routes: the fixed header, the footer, decorative spacer bands and the cookie-consent root.
categories.HERO: The page-opening block: the h1 and its immediate supporting copy, CTAs and hero visual.
categories.PROOF: Third-party credibility: customer logos, named outcome metrics, testimonials, compliance badges.
categories.FEATURES: Explanatory product content — capability grids, stepped walkthroughs, interactive showcases.
categories.NARRATIVE: Prose-led blocks: problem/solution framings, case-study bodies, article bodies, legal clauses.
categories.INDEX: A list of links to other routes.
categories.CTA: A conversion band whose only job is to move the visitor to a demo.

cta.book-demo-band.description: Full-bleed dark-navy conversion band: the arced 'rubie' wordmark, the headline 'Your customers are waiting on data that lives behind a login.' and one Book a Demo button.
cta.book-demo-band.scope: 19 routes — all but /privacy-policy and /terms, which end at their legal body.

cta.story-email-capture.description: The story sidebar's conversion card: the site mark, one line of copy, a work-email input and a 'Get started' submit button (submit is prevented in the clone).
cta.story-email-capture.scope: The 5 /customers/<name> routes (sticky sidebar, under the company facts).

faq.accordion.description: 'Your questions answered' — a question-and-answer accordion. Byte-identical on all six use-case routes, so the same questions are asked regardless of vertical.

features.any-source.description: 'Any source. Your platform.' — the source-connector capability block with its animated source-to-target diagram.

features.automation-samples.description: 'A sampling of what Integration Playbooks automate today' — a list of concrete automations shipped.

features.capability-grid.description: A heading plus a three-item capability grid with supporting icons — the 'what you get' block.

features.enterprise-pillars.description: 'Security & Compliance First' — the enterprise assurance block covering compliance, residency, access control and audit, over a large animated backdrop.

features.pipeline-steps.description: A numbered walkthrough of the data pipeline ('01 — Authenticate' through Load), one stage per heading with an illustration each.

features.platform-primitives.description: 'Platform primitives' — an interactive tabbed showcase of the core platform capabilities, with an animated panel per tab.

features.playbook-cta-cards.description: 'Build data playbooks with Rubie' — two linked cards routing to Migration Playbooks and Integration Playbooks.

features.solution-anatomy.description: An interactive stepped anatomy of a Rubie migration — buttons stepping through the pipeline stages.

features.solution-outcomes.description: The long outcome-explainer block ('What changes when migrations just work' / 'Engineering-grade infrastructure, no engineering required') with an animated supporting visual.

features.use-case-teasers.description: 'How teams are using Rubie today' — a grid teasing the six /use-cases/* routes.

hero.article.description: Blog-post masthead: the article h1, byline/date and hero illustration.

hero.customer-story.description: Customer-story hero: one long outcome-metric h1 ('X cuts Y by Z% with Rubie'), the customer's logo and a back-link to /customers.

hero.home.description: Homepage hero: h1 'Rip and Replace your Competition', the zero-effort-migrations sub-paragraph, dual CTAs, the Rive product animation and the 58-logo customer plate.

hero.page-title.description: Minimal title-only hero — an h1 and a short standfirst, for pages whose value is the body below rather than the opening pitch.

hero.solution.description: Solutions hero: h1 naming the playbook family, supporting copy, CTA and a large inline animated diagram of the playbook pipeline.

hero.use-case.description: Use-case hero: a two-part h1 (a bold claim plus a lighter 'without ...' qualifier), supporting paragraph, CTA and the 54-logo customer plate. Identical structure on all six routes; only copy changes.

index.article-toc.description: The article's in-page table of contents: one anchor link per chapter, pointing at that chapter's #id.

index.blog-roll.description: The blog index listing — a linked card per post with title, excerpt and date.

narrative.article-chapter.description: One chapter of a long-form article: an h2 with its #id anchor, prose paragraphs and bullet points, and optional h3 cards (timeline stages, principles).
narrative.article-chapter.scope: The 1 /blog/<slug> route (one per chapter with an #id anchor).

narrative.article-sources.description: The article's closing sources list: an h2 'Sources' and one line per cited report.

narrative.legal-clause.description: One heading-bounded clause of a legal document: the numbered h2 and the paragraphs and nested list items under it, up to the next h2.
narrative.legal-clause.scope: The 2 legal routes, /privacy-policy and /terms (one per numbered clause heading).

narrative.legal-header.description: Opening of a legal document: the h1 title, the effective / last-updated date line and the preamble paragraph that names the parties and scope.
narrative.legal-header.scope: The 2 legal routes, /privacy-policy and /terms (one per page).

narrative.problem-statement.description: A short, punchy problem framing under the hero — one h2 claim ('Your customers' data is locked up in legacy systems.', 'Onboarding is your bottleneck.') with brief elaborations.
narrative.problem-statement.scope: 9 routes: /, the six /use-cases/* routes and the two /solutions/* routes.

narrative.result-callout.description: A kicker-labelled callout ('// The Result //') above one summarising sentence of at most 13 words.

narrative.solution-statement.description: The paired answer to narrative.problem-statement — an h2 resolution plus a large supporting animated visual.

narrative.story-beat.description: One chapter of a customer story (Challenge, Solution or Results): a mono eyebrow label, an h2, prose paragraphs and an optional inline customer quote.
narrative.story-beat.scope: The 5 /customers/<name> routes (the Challenge, Solution and Results beats).

proof.compliance-badges.description: A row of compliance and security badges (SOC 2 Type II and peers) under a short assurance heading.

proof.story-company-facts.description: The story sidebar's company profile: the customer's name, a one-line description and labelled facts (headquarters, employees, industry, previous solution) shown as pills.
proof.story-company-facts.scope: The 5 /customers/<name> routes (sticky sidebar, beside the story beats at >= lg).

proof.story-grid.description: A grid of customer-story cards linking to each /customers/<name> route, each carrying the customer logo and its headline outcome metric.

proof.story-metrics.description: The customer-story metric strip — three named outcome numbers with a caption each (e.g. '3 min / Per account data entry (down from 2+ hrs)'). No heading of its own.

proof.story-pull-quote.description: The customer story's opening pull quote: one italic customer quote with the speaker's name and title.

proof.testimonials.description: 'What our customers are saying' — a grid of quote cards, each with an avatar, a name, a role and the customer's logo.

shell.consent-banner-root.description: The c15t cookie-consent banner mount point and its Accept/Reject card. Third-party vendor UI mounted outside <main>, not Rubie design surface.

shell.footer.description: Site footer: four link columns (Product, Solutions, Company, Legal), the arced 'rubie' SVG wordmark and the copyright line.
shell.footer.scope: All 21 routes. Identical apart from generated SVG arc ids.

shell.header.description: Fixed top header: Rubie wordmark, primary nav (Product, Solutions, Use Cases, Resources) with hover mega-panels, and a Book a Demo button.
shell.header.scope: All 21 routes. Byte-identical on every one.

shell.spacer.description: A decorative aria-hidden="true" band with no content at all — a bordered gap the layout uses as a rule between sections. Measured copy on both instances is zero words; it must never be given any.
shell.spacer.scope: 2 routes: /blog and /solutions/migration-playbooks. Each sits in its own template now, so template membership and real route count agree.

templates.name: Legal document
templates.note: The only template with no cta.book-demo-band — both legal routes end at their document body. A measured exception, not an omission.
